references.text: Moses complains to the Lord in a similar way and asks why he has done evil to the people, a parallel to his complaint in Numbers.
Moses appeals to the Lord and asks him to turn away from his anger, which shows his role as an intercessor and the burden he carries for the people.
Moses asks to find favor in the Lord's eyes, the same expression used in Numbers 11:11.
The continuation of Moses' complaint where he expresses that the burden of carrying the people is too heavy for him alone.
Moses reminds the people that he alone could not bear the burden and strife with them, a reflection on the situation in Numbers 11.
Elijah complains to the Lord in a similar way and asks to die, a parallel to Moses' frustration over his service.
Job asks God why he has made him a target, a similar complaint about suffering directed at God.
Jonah becomes angry and complains to the Lord, a prophetic complaint that resembles Moses' frustration.
